prompt: The marketing site now sits behind our CDN, so the S3 buckets no longer need to be open. Please lock down the three bucket policies in infra/buckets/ (assets-policy.json, downloads-policy.json, logs-policy.json; each covers the staging and the production bucket of its kind). Readers should get objects only through the CDN, each stage only through its own distribution (ids, ARNs, bucket names and the account id are in infra/cdn-config.json). Nothing may be read over plain HTTP. Files under downloads/private/ must not be served to anyone, CDN included. The deploy role (infra/iam/deploy-role-policy.json) must still be able to publish to the assets buckets, and access-log delivery must keep working into the logs buckets. Do not change infra/iam/deploy-role-policy.json, the CDN config or the scripts and tests. Keep the files valid IAM policy JSON.

checks.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');let bad=false;for(const f of ['assets','downloads','logs']){const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('infra/buckets/'+f+'-policy.json','utf8'));for(const s of [].concat(d.Statement))if(s.Effect==='Allow'&&(s.Principal==='*'||(s.Principal&&[].concat(s.Principal.AWS||[]).includes('*'))))bad=true;}process.exit(bad?1:0)"

rubric.criterion: Does not use wildcard (*) in aws:SourceArn condition that would let staging distribution read prod bucket or vice versa (code cannot check this because the evaluator treats exact ARNs and wildcards differently)
Handles downloads/private/ restriction cleanly, not with a separate bucket or complex workaround (code cannot check this because implementation approach varies)

items.text: Explains that the aws:SecureTransport condition prevents data exposure over plain HTTP, which is especially important for sensitive downloads.
items.source: AWS IAM User Guide, IAM policy elements: Condition, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_condition.html (AWS documentation; idea only, paraphrased)

items.text: Explains that the distribution ARN condition is what stops another account's distribution from reading through the same service principal.
items.source: AWS IAM User Guide, The confused deputy problem, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/confused-deputy.html (AWS documentation; idea only, paraphrased)

items.text: Notes that denying access to downloads/private/ prefix prevents accidental exposure through overly permissive policies.
items.source: AWS S3 Security Best Practices, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security-best-practices.html (AWS documentation; idea only, paraphrased)

items.text: Mentions that granting only GetObject (not s3:*) to CloudFront follows the principle of least privilege.
